segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also in me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places. If there were not, I would have told you, because I am going to prepare a place for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And you know the way to where I am going.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thomas said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on you know him and have seen him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, show us the Father, and that is enough for us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have I been with all of you for so long, and you have not come to know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I say to you I do not speak on my own; the Father who remains in me does his works.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or else, believe because of the works themselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whatever you ask in my name, that I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you love me, you will keep my commandments.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever—

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, because he remains with you and will be in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In a little while the world will no longer see me, but you will see me. Because I live, you also will live.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. And the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I too will love them and reveal myself to them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judas—not Iscariot—said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, what has happened, that you are going to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If anyone loves me, they will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our dwelling with them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but belongs to the Father who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name—he will teach you everything and remind you of everything I have said to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Peace I leave with you; my own peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them lose courage.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You heard me tell you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I will not speak with you much longer, for the ruler of the world is coming. He has no claim on me,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but so that the world may know that I love the Father, I do just as the Father commanded me. Get up; let us go from here.”

notes.phrase: Believe in God; believe also in me.
notes.traditional: ye believe in God, believe also in me
notes.note: The Greek verb form is the same for a statement (“you believe”) and a command (“believe”), and it occurs twice. The line can therefore be read as two commands, as here, or as “You believe in God; believe also in me,” or even as two statements. Most recent translations and commentators take both as commands, which suits the opening “Do not let your hearts be troubled.”

The Greek noun means a place where one stays or lives and is related to the verb translated “remain” throughout this chapter. “Mansions” comes from the Latin translation, where the word meant a lodging, and now wrongly suggests a grand house. Many modern versions have “rooms.” “Dwelling places” is used here so that the link with verse 23, where the same noun is rendered “dwelling,” stays visible.

notes.phrase: I would have told you, because I am going
notes.traditional: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you
notes.note: The Greek can be punctuated in more than one way. It may be a question: “If there were not, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?” Many recent versions take it so. This translation follows the punctuation of the edition being translated, which reads it as a statement, and takes the connecting word as “because.”

notes.phrase: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also.
notes.traditional: If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also
notes.note: Manuscripts differ here. The reading translated is a mild rebuke that implies the disciples have not really known Jesus. Other early manuscripts read “If you have come to know me, you will know my Father also,” which is a promise. Scholars are divided over which is original.

notes.traditional: If ye shall ask any thing in my name
notes.note: Some manuscripts lack “me,” and a few omit the whole verse, probably because it seemed to repeat verse 13. The reading with “me,” in which prayer is addressed to Jesus himself, has strong early support and is the one translated.

Outside the New Testament the word is used of someone called in to speak or act on another’s behalf, and 1 John 2:1 uses it of Jesus in just that sense. “Comforter” goes back to early English versions and is narrower than the Greek. “Advocate,” “Helper” and “Counselor” are all in current use among translators. “Another” implies that Jesus himself has been filling this role for the disciples.

The Greek word for “Spirit” is grammatically neuter, and the pronouns in this verse are neuter to agree with it. In verse 26 the pronoun is masculine, agreeing with the masculine noun for “Advocate.” Greek grammatical gender does not itself indicate personhood. English “whom” and “him” follow the long-standing tradition and fit the personal role the Spirit is given in this passage.

notes.phrase: but you will see me. Because I live, you also will live.
notes.traditional: but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also
notes.note: The Greek can also be read as one sentence: “but you will see me, because I live and you will live.” On that reading the disciples’ seeing Jesus is grounded in his life and theirs. The translation follows the more common division, which makes “Because I live, you also will live” a separate promise.

This verb is not the ordinary Greek word for fear. It means to be timid or cowardly, to lose one’s nerve. The Greek Old Testament uses it in exhortations such as those to Joshua not to be dismayed before a daunting task. Most English versions have simply “be afraid.”

notes.phrase: He has no claim on me
notes.note: The Greek is literally “in me he has nothing.” Most interpreters take this as an idiom meaning that the ruler of the world has no claim on Jesus or hold over him, perhaps reflecting a Semitic legal expression. Several modern versions also render it “no claim on me” or “no power over me.”

notes.phrase: but so that the world may know
notes.traditional: But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do
notes.note: The Greek sentence is compressed and has no stated main clause before “so that.” It can be read as here, with “I do just as the Father commanded me” as the main statement. It can also be read as “but this happens so that the world may know that I love the Father and that I do just as the Father commanded me.” The sense differs only slightly.

notes.phrase: Get up; let us go from here.
notes.note: Jesus’ speech nevertheless continues for three more chapters, and the group is not said to leave until 18:1. Some scholars think the following chapters were spoken on the way. Others think the line marks a seam where different blocks of discourse were joined, or that it is a summons to face what is coming rather than to leave the room. The question is unresolved.

Recurs with commandments and word across John, 1 John and Revelation, where translators alternate between “keep,” “obey” and “observe.”
Frequent in John and Paul; translators vary between “glorify,” “honor” and “bring glory to,” and the link with δόξα should stay visible.
Used of Jesus’ own distress (John 11:33, 12:27, 13:21) and of the disciples’ hearts here; one rendering would keep that echo audible.
